author: Vincent Chow
description:
The unique circumstances surrounding Huawei Technologies’ landmark trial in a US court made jury selection especially important to ensuring a fair trial for the Chinese tech giant, according to US litigation experts.
Known as voir dire, the process allows the presiding judge and two legal teams to question prospective jurors before the trial begins to identify possible bias and conflicts that could impede their ability to adjudicate the case in a “fair and impartial” way.
Richard Gabriel,...
title: Huawei’s US trial puts jury to the test amid China, Iran links

author: Igor Patrick
description:
China has warned Panama of “serious consequences” after most of the country’s lawmakers set up a parliamentary exchange group with Taiwan, defying pressure from Beijing’s embassy and a public disavowal by their own president.
The warning came from foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun, who said on Monday that the group seriously violated the one-China principle upheld by Panama and urged what he called “those few politicians” to “see the real picture”.
Beijing had noted the Panamanian...
title: Beijing threatens ‘serious consequences’ after Panama lawmakers support Taiwan

author: dpa
description:
Germany’s military counter-intelligence agency, known as MAD, has warned of a growing threat from hybrid attacks and the use of recruited contract agents, or low-level agents, saying Germany is a “prioritised target of Russian espionage activities”.
According to the agency’s annual report released on Monday, it cited Germany’s geostrategic position in Europe and Nato the expansion of the Bundeswehr and the introduction of new weapons systems as reasons for the heightened targeting.
“The hybrid...
title: German intelligence report warns of rising Chinese, Russian spy threat

author: Lucy Quaggin
description:
US President Donald Trump downplayed growing concerns about artificial intelligence on Monday, claiming America already has guardrails to regulate the industry and warning that casting doubt on development only benefits China.
“The only control or ‘guardrails’ ‌that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades!” Trump wrote on social media.
“We already have tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these ⁠companies! There is a SICK conspiracy going...
title: Trump condemns ‘sick conspiracy’ against AI, says he is only guardrail needed

author: Khushboo Razdan,Cao Jiaxuan
description:
The family photograph did the political work the summit’s final declaration could not.
Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian leader Vladimir Putin, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi stood shoulder to shoulder as the Brics summit closed in New Delhi on Sunday – a single frame capturing an 11-nation bloc that now spans four continents and nearly half the world’s population.
UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres attended the gathering of emerging economies...
title: Brics leaders act to hedge – not revolt – against US dollar dominance

author: Meredith Chen
description:
President Donald Trump’s claim that the new White House ballroom will top China’s Great Hall of the People has thrust the Beijing landmark back into the spotlight just as Chinese President Xi Jinping prepares for his US visit later this month.
Speaking at a Republican midterm convention in Dallas last week, Trump described the Great Hall of the People – China’s most prestigious venue for legislative and ceremonial events – as “a serious hall”.
“This is a very large hall, but we’re going to top...
title: Can Trump’s White House ballroom top China’s vast Great Hall of the People?

author: Tang Meng Kit
description:
Uzbekistan’s recent confirmation that China’s J-10CE fighters have entered into service in its air force ended months of speculation. It is the latest of three developments that include Pakistan’s use of J-10CEs in combat last year and Bangladesh’s draft procurement paper for the Chinese aircraft.
Read separately, each looks like a win for the J-10CE. Taken together, however, they show something narrower: the Chinese aircraft is gaining export traction without yet winning a clean contest against...
title: China’s J-10CE has foreign buyers, but not yet a market

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Guangzhou police apprehended a man in the southern Chinese city’s university town district after receiving reports that he was wielding a knife and injuring pedestrians, according to a police statement.
According to an alert by the Panyu district branch of the Guangzhou Municipal Public Security Bureau, at about 5.20pm local time, emergency services received calls about multiple stabbings in front of a hotpot restaurant in the district’s Xiaoguwei Island.
The bureau said in a social media post...
title: Knife attack in China’s Guangzhou university town leaves multiple people injured

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Taiwan’s military has taken delivery of 291 one-way attack drones from US maker Anduril Industries, only to find they came without chargers and require American assistance to recharge them.
The revelation involving the Altius-600M loitering munitions has prompted Taiwan’s opposition lawmakers to question the military’s procurement and logistical planning, days before the drones join other weapons systems in a three-day live-fire exercise.
The controversy comes at a sensitive time in...
title: Taiwan defence logistics under fire over missing chargers for US drones

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Japan is looking to develop submarine-detecting quantum sensors for aerial drones, the latest move in a growing undersea competition pitting China against the United States and its allies across the Indo-Pacific.
Released in late August, Tokyo’s defence budget request for fiscal 2027 includes research into a smaller, more capable quantum magnetic sensor, a technology that uses the properties of atoms to detect tiny changes in magnetic fields that could reveal a submarine.
The project is one of...
title: Japan eyes quantum sub-hunting drone sensors as China extends undersea reach

author: Brian Rhoads,Raymond Ma
description:
President Xi Jinping promoted China’s vision for artificial intelligence (AI) at the annual Brics summit, seeking to win support from the Global South amid tech competition with the US.
China would spearhead development of an AI Brics “community”, support cooperation in developing large language models and offer training, Xi said on Sunday in New Delhi. The previous day, he invited Brics nations to join the newly formed World AI Cooperation Organisation.
Brics countries must “strengthen...
title: Xi touts Brics cooperation on AI as US titans flag tech risks

author: Alcott Wei
description:
Beijing has hailed a “one country, two systems” proposal by a Taiwanese scholar in a rare official statement on an issue regarded as politically sensitive on both sides of the Taiwan Strait.
“We are pleased to see that more and more Taiwan compatriots are facing up to reunification, beginning to understand and discuss the specific content of a one country, two systems plan for Taiwan, and offering suggestions and proposals for such a plan through various means,” Chen Binhua, a spokesman for...
title: Beijing hails Taiwanese scholar’s rare proposal on reunification

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Scientists have developed a lightweight, battery-free device that could help improve the mobility of people with difficulty walking, such as stroke survivors.
Developed by researchers in Hong Kong and mainland China, the neural prosthesis uses energy generated by the wearer’s own movements to electrically stimulate their muscles, helping to flex their ankle and restore their natural walking pattern.
This could prevent falls for stroke survivors, elderly individuals, and others living with...
title: China’s self-powered neural device helps stroke survivors walk naturally

author: Dannie Peng
description:
Beijing has introduced stricter drone regulations, banning all uncrewed flights as well as the possession and storage of existing devices, while detailing disposal methods for the first time in an effort to strengthen security in the capital.
The new rules, which will take effect on November 15, follow an incident in June, when a small aircraft crashed into Beijing’s tallest building, the Citic Tower – also known as China Zun – leading to the death of the pilot.
The newly revised regulations on...
title: Beijing puts a total ban on drones in update to regulations after deadly crash

author: Meredith Chen
description:
For generations of Chinese schoolchildren, English textbooks offered a glimpse of an unfamiliar world, from London’s Tower Bridge and Big Ben to American school life and Halloween traditions.
Today, students opening an English textbook are more likely to encounter passages on late Qing dynasty (1644-1912) thinker Liang Qichao, the Dragon Boat Festival and China’s overseas aid projects.
These changes are part of a nationwide overhaul of China’s primary and middle-school textbooks, which have...
title: Are Chinese students learning English just to ‘tell China’s story’?

author: Carol Yang
description:
China could improve its image in the United States by highlighting areas such as tourism and technology and positioning itself as a responsible major power, a survey has concluded.
Researchers from Sun Yat-sen University in Guangzhou said that although concepts such as “decoupling” and “de-risking” had been increasingly prominent in media coverage of China, this had not entirely wiped away positive impressions of the country.
When evaluating China’s strengths on a scale of 1 to 5, the...
title: Tourism and technology may hold key to boosting China’s public image in the US

author: John Lee Ka-chiu
description:
This year marks the opening year of the national 15th five-year plan. Faced with accelerating change globally and significant opportunities brought by national development, Hong Kong must better integrate into and serve the overall national development, enabling our economic progress to reach new heights while enhancing people’s livelihood and well-being.
This February, I announced that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government would formulate the city’s first five-year plan. I led...
title: How the 5-year plan can serve the nation and deliver for Hong Kong

author: Carol Yang
description:
China’s top intelligence official has warned of rising national security risks posed by artificial intelligence (AI), calling for robust risk prevention frameworks and stronger global governance of the emerging technology.
The call from Chen Yixin, China’s state security minister, comes as Beijing seeks to play a leading role in global AI governance while criticising US restrictions. At the Brics summit in India over the weekend, Chinese President Xi Jinping proposed an AI-powered initiative to...
title: China’s intelligence chief warns of risks from AI as ‘new arena for strategic rivalry’
